# Client-Side Handling

Covers Dimension 7: How API consumers parse and act on problem details.

See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## RFC 9457 Client Requirements

The specification defines how consumers MUST handle problem details [1]:

| Requirement | Normative Level |
|-------------|----------------|
| Use `type` URI as primary problem identifier | MUST [1] |
| Ignore unrecognized extension members | MUST [1] |
| Ignore members whose value type doesn't match | MUST [1] |
| NOT automatically dereference type URI | SHOULD NOT [1] |
| NOT parse `detail` for machine logic | SHOULD NOT [1] |
| Resolve relative URIs per RFC 3986 §5 | Required [1] |

Key principle: `type` is the stable identifier for programmatic handling;
`detail` is for human consumption only [1].

## Client Libraries

### JavaScript/TypeScript

| Library | Description | RFC Version |
|---------|-------------|-------------|
| http-problem-details [21] | ProblemDocument class, TypeScript typings, URI validation | RFC 7807 |
| http-problem-details-parser | Client-side parsing with type guards | RFC 7807 |
| http-problem-details-mapper | Error-to-problem mapping by convention | RFC 7807 |
| @curveball/http-errors | TypeScript HTTP exceptions with problem+json | RFC 9457 |

**http-problem-details** usage [21]:

```javascript
const { ProblemDocument, ProblemDocumentExtension } = require('http-problem-details');

// Creating a problem document
const doc = new ProblemDocument({
  type: 'https://example.com/probs/out-of-credit',
  title: 'Insufficient credit balance',
  detail: 'Current balance is 30, but transaction costs 50.',
  instance: '/account/12345/msgs/abc',
  status: 400
});

// With extensions
const extension = new ProblemDocumentExtension({
  balance: 30,
  accounts: ['/account/12345', '/account/67890']
});
const doc = new ProblemDocument({...}, extension);
```

Key behaviors [21]:
- If only `status` is provided, `type` defaults to `about:blank` and `title`
  becomes the HTTP reason phrase (e.g., "Not Found" for 404)
- Both `type` and `instance` are validated as proper URIs

Python ecosystem observation: most Python libraries are framework-specific

## Client Parsing Patterns

### Content-Type Detection

Clients should check the response Content-Type header before parsing [1]:

```javascript
// Fetch API pattern
const response = await fetch(url);
if (!response.ok) {
  const contentType = response.headers.get('content-type');
  if (contentType?.includes('application/problem+json') ||
      contentType?.includes('application/json')) {
    const problem = await response.json();
    // Handle structured problem details
  }
}
```

### Axios vs Fetch Handling

| Aspect | Fetch API | Axios |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| Error detection | Manual: check `response.ok` | Automatic: rejects on non-2xx |
| JSON parsing | Manual: `response.json()` | Automatic: `error.response.data` |
| Content-Type check | Manual | Manual |

Axios automatically rejects promises for non-2xx statuses, simplifying problem
details handling compared to Fetch where manual checking is required [19].

### Error Recovery Based on Problem Type

The `type` URI enables programmatic error handling [1] [3]:

```javascript
switch (problem.type) {
  case 'https://example.com/rate-limited':
    if (problem.retryable && problem.retry_after) {
      await delay(problem.retry_after * 1000);
      return retry(request);
    }
    break;
  case 'https://example.com/validation-error':
    highlightFields(problem.errors);
    break;
}
```

Cloudflare's `retryable` and `retry_after` extensions enable automated retry
logic without custom per-API code [3].

## Instance Field and Correlation

The `instance` field identifies a specific problem occurrence [1]:

- Cloudflare uses the Ray ID as the instance value [3]
- Many implementations use extension fields (`correlationId`, `traceId`) rather
  than the standard `instance` field for distributed tracing correlation
- A correlation ID tracks one request end-to-end; a trace ID is the root
  identifier grouping all spans across services

ASP.NET Core's `CustomizeProblemDetails` can inject a TraceId extension to
correlate client errors with server logs [20].

## Gaps and Limitations

- No comprehensive client library for RFC 9457 in JavaScript — most libraries
  implement RFC 7807 only [21]
- Python client ecosystem is framework-coupled; no general-purpose RFC 9457
  parser for consuming APIs
- No standard mechanism for clients to discover available extension members
- Limited guidance on how clients should handle `type` URIs that change
  (problem type evolution)
- No published benchmarks comparing client library parsing performance
